"As an artist you actually do have to make a choice to be an outsider. If you're an outsider you have the freedom to say what people on the inside don't dare to say," she stated to CNN. After studying acting in France and Italy and debuting in a 1984 French film, her international breakthrough came with Ridley Scott's 2000 "Gladiator," where she played Lucilla opposite Russell Crowe and Joaquin Phoenix. Despite this success, Nielsen actively resisted typecasting into "love interest" roles, criticizing Hollywood's gender disparity: "It's unjust" to face limited roles after proving capability. Nielsen emphasizes she reveals the human dimensions of conflict without making overt political statements. She stresses that acting is not her life's focus, prioritizing time with family, literature, and art, stating, "I will always find something that I want to try and become better at. I always love to spend more time with my friends, more time with my family." Her commitment to artistic integrity, engagement with social themes, and disavowal of Hollywood celebrity distinguish her career path, rooted in principle rather than industry expectations.
